title: Reconciliation Talks Deliver Concrete Progress for Venezuela’s Democratic Transition
summary_raw:
Office of the Spokesman
Fact Sheet


			
			


			
			
October 9, 2026

Political reconciliation talks between the interim Venezuelan government and 2015 National Assembly representatives are producing tangible reforms in civil liberties and political rights, laying the groundwork for credible elections and a democratic transition.  Two rounds of talks have already taken place, producing significant results:  a wholesale reform and reconstruction of an independent Venezuelan Supreme Court, the restoration of access to more than 70 previously blocked internet domains, and the reform of a key repressive law.  The interim government has also released more than 1,000 political prisoners and announced the release of nearly 200 more.   
The talks bring together representatives of Venezuela’s 2015 National Assembly, led by its President Dinorah Figuera, and representatives of the interim government, led by current National Assembly President Jorge Rodríguez.  The 2015 National Assembly was Venezuela’s last democratically elected legislative body recognized by all Venezuelan political parties and by the international community.   
The delegations held two rounds of talks in Caracas in August and September, with another round scheduled to begin October 14.  The parties have decided to remain in session to maintain the momentum they have achieved.  
The United States supports this Venezuelan-led process to create the conditions for a peaceful democratic transition, which is only possible because of President Trump’s bold leadership. Early accomplishments include the following: 
Rebuilding an Independent Supreme Court:
Following the talks, the 2026 National Assembly published a law reforming the Supreme Court selection process, with 32 new judges to be selected by December.  The Supreme Court will adjudicate any challenges to Venezuela’s future election results, underscoring the importance of a credible selection process. 
The talks led to the creation of a seven-member Credentials Council, an unprecedented all-judge body that will screen candidates and send only qualified jurists to the Judicial Nominations Committee.  Importantly, the 2015 National Assembly chose a majority of the Council. 
The Judicial Nominations Committee, made up of 11 current National Assembly members and 12 civil society members, will choose the 32 nominees from the Credentials Council’s approved list. 
This selection process increases transparency and enshrines protections to ensure the new judges will be qualified and not tied to the Maduro regime. 
Expanding Freedom of Expression:
The interim government has restored or partially restored access to more than 70 previously blocked internet domains, including El Tiempo, EFE, Revista Semana, El Pitazo, Efecto Cucuyo, among others. 
Reforming Repressive Laws:
The National Assembly established a commission to reform and decriminalize penalties contained in the repressive 2017 Law Against Hatred, which was notorious for its use by the Maduro regime to jail opposition leaders and those who spoke out against the regime. 
The law established penalties of up to 20 years in prison for the “promotion or incitement of hatred, discrimination, or violence,” although in practice it was used to punish criticism of the regime.   
Releasing Political Prisoners: 
The interim government has released over 1,000 political prisoners since Operation Absolute Resolve.  Since the political reconciliation talks began in August, the interim government has announced the release of an additional 177 political prisoners, an important step toward restoring fundamental political freedoms.   
Prominent political prisoners released since January 3 include Juan Pablo Guanipa, advisor to Maria Corina Machado and former First Vice President of the National Assembly; Freddy Superlano, ex-gubernatorial candidate and former National Assembly member; and Enrique Márquez, ex-presidential candidate and former Vice President of the National Electoral Council. 
Exiled opposition figures Claudia Macero and Omar González Moreno, who fled the threat of detention due to political motivated charges, have also returned to Venezuela.  
What Comes Next  
The third round of reconciliation talks is scheduled to begin October 14.  The delegations will focus on finalizing the Supreme Court selection process and providing individuals and political parties participation guarantees necessary for credible elections.   
Future rounds of dialogue will address reform of the National Electoral Council, repealing remaining repressive laws, and opening political space so all political parties and leaders can return and participate in political life.   
We welcome the joint efforts with Venezuela’s interim government to recover the gold in the United Kingdom. 
The Trump Administration will continue to support this Venezuelan-led process as it moves from dialogue to durable democratic institutions. 
For media inquiries, please contact the Office of the Spokesman.

title: Secretary Rubio’s Meeting with Venezuela’s 2015 National Assembly President Dinorah Figuera
summary_raw:
Office of the Spokesman
Readout


			
			


			
			
October 9, 2026

Secretary of State Marco Rubio met today in Washington with Venezuela’s 2015 National Assembly President Dinorah Figuera. 
The Secretary commended Figuera’s courageous leadership in advancing political reconciliation following Operation Absolute Resolve and welcomed the tangible progress achieved during the first two rounds of talks with the interim authorities.  He highlighted this year’s steps toward establishing an independent Supreme Court of Justice, the release of over 1,200 political prisoners, the recently restored access to blocked media websites, and efforts to reform the Law Against Hatred as important milestones toward restoring fundamental freedoms for the Venezuelan people. 
Looking ahead to the next round of talks beginning October 14, the Secretary urged continued progress on political freedoms and electoral reform, which would lay the groundwork for free, fair, and credible elections in Venezuela.  Both reaffirmed their commitment to building on the momentum of the talks and translating this historic opportunity into lasting democratic change for the Venezuelan people.

title: Secretary of State Marco Rubio and 2015 Venezuelan National Assembly President Dinorah Figuera Before Their Meeting
summary_raw:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
Dinorah Figuera, 2015 Venezuelan National Assembly President
Washington, D.C.
Harry S. Truman Building
Remarks


			
			


			
			
October 9, 2026








SECRETARY RUBIO:  Let me just say a few words, please.  First of all, I want to welcome Dr. Figuera here to the United States.  She has our 100 percent support.  Our desire for Venezuela is that it not just simply have elections; elections, of course, are very important to have a democracy, an enduring democracy.  This is a country that’s recovering from almost a quarter century of trauma, a very big trauma, and this is the best opportunity Venezuela has had, almost in a generation, not just to have elections that are free and fair, but in addition to leave behind an enduring democracy for future generations.  This is going to involve the participation – it has to involve the participation of every sector of society. 
And I want to leave it abundantly clear that this process that she is leading, along with her team, has 100 percent support, the strongest possible support from the highest levels of our government.  And we encourage everyone who cares about the future of Venezuela to participate in this process in a way that’s positive.  They have already achieved concrete results; more results will be necessary. 
But to have a peaceful transition – which is what we desire, a peaceful transition to a permanent and enduring democracy – will require a lot of hard work, a little bit of patience, free and fair elections, but more than just free and fair elections, the institutions that don’t just sustain democracy, but sustain stability and progress and prosperity and freedom for the people of Venezuela for the foreseeable future. 
(In Spanish.)
Muchísimas gracias.  Thank you for covering this.  Thank you. 
QUESTION:  When do you expect elections, Mr. Secretary?
QUESTION:  (In Spanish.)
SECRETARY RUBIO:  Perdón.  I’m sorry.
MS FIGUERA:  (In Spanish.)
QUESTION:  (In Spanish.)
QUESTION:  Is there a timeline set?
MS FIGUERA:  (In Spanish.)
QUESTION:  (In Spanish.)
MS FIGUERA:  Gracias.

title: Fiji National Day
summary_raw:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
Press Statement


			
			


			
			
October 9, 2026

On behalf of the United States of America, I extend my warmest congratulations to the people of Fiji as you celebrate your national day.
Today is an opportunity to honor Fiji’s rich history and cultural heritage. The United States values our strong partnership with Fiji, built on our shared commitment to prosperity, peace, and security in the Pacific. Our ongoing work together through the Millennium Challenge Corporation is laying the foundation for the U.S.-Fiji partnership to reach new heights in years to come. We appreciate Fiji’s important contributions to the region, and we look forward to deepening our collaboration in the years ahead.
I wish you a prosperous and joyous Fiji Day.

title: Imposing Sanctions on the International Criminal Court
summary_raw:
Office of the Spokesman
Fact Sheet


			
			


			
			
October 9, 2026
Under President Trump, the United States has acted decisively to defend U.S. sovereignty and U.S. citizens against the threat of the International Criminal Court (ICC).  To date, the United States has imposed sanctions on 17 persons pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 14203 “Imposing Sanctions on the International Criminal Court.”  Today, the Department of State announces additional actions to defend U.S. sovereignty and neutralize the threat posed by the ICC. 
The ICC is being designated pursuant to section 1(a)(ii)(A) of Executive Order 14203.*
Concurrent with this designation, the Department of the Treasury is issuing a set of general licenses (GLs) authorizing certain transactions involving the ICC to protect U.S. interests.


A 180-day GL authorizing certain activity involving the ICC, including for the maintenance of its operations;
A GL authorizing certain IT-related activities, including cloud and software services;
A GL authorizing activity related to the ICC pension plan; and
A GL authorizing certain activity related to the ICC detainees.  





For more details please reference OFAC’s website.
The 180-day maintenance GL is intended to provide time for States Parties to demonstrate meaningful progress on diplomatic and legal resolutions that address fundamental U.S. concerns regarding the ICC. This GL can be adjusted in response to the success or failure of such efforts to address our concerns.   
Watch Secretary Rubio’s video message announcing U.S. sanctions on the ICC on the Department of State’s YouTube channel.
* Sanctions Implications
As a result of today’s sanctions-related actions, and subject to applicable licenses and exceptions, all property and interests in property of the ICC that are in the United States or in possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to the Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC).
All transactions by U.S. persons or within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of designated or otherwise blocked persons are prohibited unless exempt or authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC, including those general licenses described above. These prohibitions include the making of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services by, to, or for the benefit of any blocked person and the receipt of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services from any such person.
Petitions for removal from the SDN List may be sent to: OFAC.Reconsideration@treasury.gov. Petitioners may also refer to the Department of State’s Delisting Guidance page.

title: Imposing Sanctions on the International Criminal Court
summary_raw:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
Press Statement


			
			


			
			
October 9, 2026

For decades, Republicans and Democrats alike rejected the idea that the International Criminal Court had the power to prosecute American citizens, military servicemembers, or political leaders. America never joined the court. We don’t need it. And we don’t want it.
But globalist “experts” an ocean away don’t care what American citizens think. They want the ICC to do more, including the prosecution of American citizens. Servicemembers defending their country, Border Patrol agents protecting our nation, and elected leaders ensuring our national security. They want more power, and they want it at our expense. 
President Trump will never allow the International Criminal Court to prosecute Americans. That is why, today, the United States is sanctioning the International Criminal Court. We will ban transactions with this rogue court, cutting off their resources and crippling its ability to operate.
We have been clear for over a year as to the basic gestures of good faith we have expected from the court. We exercised discretion and deferred this designation out of respect for our relationships and in hopes that the ICC would change course or would otherwise be restrained by States Parties. However, neither the ICC nor States Parties have yet taken meaningful steps to address our concerns. 
Despite their inaction, we hold out hope for a diplomatic solution. We have structured this action to provide an opportunity for States Parties to negotiate and present a solution to address our concerns. If these efforts do not bear fruit, we will continue to adjust accordingly.
Our message is clear: the United States and its people are not subject to the jurisdiction of the ICC. Both parties agree on this, but only President Trump has the resolve to take the action needed to end this threat for good. Either the ICC will end its threats, or we will end the ICC. We expect our allies, many of whom are part of the ICC and that rely on American servicemembers for their defense, to rein in the court.
If they do not, the United States will continue its campaign to dismantle the ICC, brick by brick, until Americans are threatened no longer.
The ICC is being designated pursuant to section 1(a)(ii)(A) of Executive Order (E.O.) 14203.

title: Uganda National Day
summary_raw:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
Press Statement


			
			


			
			
October 9, 2026

On behalf of the United States of America, I congratulate the people of Uganda on the 64th anniversary of Uganda’s independence and wish them a happy Independence Day.
The shared bond between the United States and Uganda is built on a foundation of respect for sovereignty and a desire to build a more prosperous future. In the past year, we have grown our commercial ties, advanced regional security and partnered to improve global public health.
I am confident the enduring partnership between the United States and Uganda will continue to flourish in the years to come bringing greater opportunity to both our peoples.
We extend our best wishes to the people of Uganda and look forward to building a stronger partnership in the coming years.
